question: A healthy 50-year-old woman asks why she needs a routine mammogram when she feels fine. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Routine screening is legally required for all women over the age of forty in this country.
options.B: Screening tests catch cancer early before symptoms develop, which makes treatment more successful.
options.C: These tests are designed to prevent normal cells from ever mutating into cancerous growths.
options.D: Mammograms are only performed after a physician feels a distinct lump during a physical exam.

explanation: Screening is all about catching things early before they turn into bigger problems. Early detection makes treatment much easier!

question: What is the purpose of performing a non-stress test in a pregnant woman with poorly controlled diabetes?

options.A: To confirm the exact gestational age of the fetus
options.B: To measure the exact amount of amniotic fluid present
options.C: To evaluate fetal heart rate patterns and oxygenation
options.D: To check if the maternal pancreas is producing insulin

explanation: A non-stress test monitors how the fetal heart rate responds to movement, which helps nurses and doctors check if the baby is getting enough oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h4)

question: What is the main danger nurses must watch out for in elderly patients undergoing heavy bowel cleansing?

options.A: Dehydration and electrolyte imbalance from losing too much fluid
options.B: High blood pressure caused by laxatives
options.C: Sudden weight gain from water holding in the skin
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the large intestine muscles

explanation: Strong laxatives and clear liquids cause quick bowel emptying, which can easily dry out and weaken older adults.

question: A patient says they feel like a dark curtain or shadow is moving across their vision. What emergency should you suspect?

options.A: Open-angle glaucoma
options.B: Nuclear cataract
options.C: Retinal detachment
options.D: Simple conjunctivitis

explanation: Spot on! That classic 'curtain falling' description is a textbook warning sign that the retina is peeling away from the back of the eye. It's a medical emergency!

question: Which simple nursing action helps relax tummy muscles and ease pain for a patient having severe cramps (colic)?

options.A: Firmly massaging the lower abdomen in circles
options.B: Placing the patient flat on their stomach with a pillow
options.C: Encouraging them to take a brisk walk around the ward
options.D: Elevating the head of the bed and bending their knees

explanation: Bending the knees takes the tension right off the abdominal wall muscles, which instantly eases up the cramping pressure. Try it yourself!

question: A clinic treats all teenagers fairly, without any bias based on religion or wealth. Which core principle is this?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Speed
options.C: Isolation
options.D: Specialization

explanation: Correct! Equity means fairness and zero discrimination—every young person gets the care they need regardless of background.

question: Why is 'trial and error' considered a risky problem-solving technique at the bedside?

options.A: It requires permission from the hospital board of directors
options.B: It can cause direct harm to the patient if the first guess is wrong
options.C: It takes too long to document in the hospital computer
options.D: It is completely forbidden by all nursing regulatory councils

explanation: Testing random solutions on a human body can lead to dangerous clinical outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the classic scan finding for a patient with Pick's disease?

options.A: Atrophy localized to the frontal and temporal lobes
options.B: Swelling and inflammation throughout the cerebellum
options.C: Multiple blocked blood vessels in the deep brain
options.D: Enlargement of the occipital cortex exclusively

explanation: Spot on! 'Atrophy' just means shrinkage. Scans of Pick's patients clearly show shrinking right in the frontal and temporal areas of the brain.

question: How do patients with neuropathic pain commonly describe what they feel?

options.A: Sharp, localized throbbing after a surgical incision
options.B: Pressure and cramping inside the abdominal cavity
options.C: Burning, shooting, or electric shock sensations
options.D: A dull, constant ache deep inside the bone

explanation: Nerve damage produces characteristic sensory disturbances like burning, tingling, or shooting pains that feel like electricity. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h2)

question: What position should your patient be in when you are inserting a nasogastric tube?

options.A: Lying on the left side (Sims position)
options.B: Sitting upright in high Fowler's position
options.C: Head tilted downward (Trendelenburg)
options.D: Flat on the back (supine)

explanation: Sitting the patient straight up aligns their throat nicely, making it much easier and safer to slide the tube down. Great job!

question: A patient has chronic open-angle glaucoma. Which part of their vision usually fades first?

options.A: Upper vertical vision only
options.B: Side (peripheral) vision
options.C: Central vision
options.D: Color vision

explanation: Correct! Open-angle glaucoma is sneaky; it slowly steals side vision first, long before the person notices any trouble with their central view.

question: Which body structure is hurt when someone suffers a sprain?

options.A: Tendon
options.B: Muscle
options.C: Cartilage
options.D: Ligament

explanation: A sprain happens when a ligament gets stretched too far or tears. Remember: ligaments connect bone to bone at your joints! You've got this.

question: How long should a patient typically fast before getting an FDG tracer injection for a PET scan?

options.A: 4 to 6 hours
options.B: No fasting is needed
options.C: 12 to 24 hours
options.D: 30 to 60 minutes

explanation: You got it! Fasting for 4 to 6 hours lowers the sugar already floating in the blood, so the cells will eagerly take up the radioactive FDG sugar instead.

question: What do we call using a traditional or home healing practice right alongside standard hospital treatment?

options.A: Alternative medicine
options.B: Biomedical intervention
options.C: Complementary therapy
options.D: Allopathic treatment

explanation: Great job! Complementary therapy means adding practices alongside regular hospital medicine, whereas alternative medicine is used to replace it completely.

question: As women grow older, which health screenings become most important?

options.A: Ovulation tracking and fertility windows
options.B: Congenital anomaly prevention counseling
options.C: Cervical and breast cancer screenings
options.D: Testicular self-examination techniques

explanation: Spot on! Regular checks for cervical changes and breast health are vital preventative steps as women age.

question: Why is continuous, long-term monitoring so essential when caring for patients with degenerative conditions?

options.A: It completely stops the underlying genetic mutation from spreading
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: It guarantees the patient will regain full physical strength
options.D: It helps catch slow, steady declines and new complications early

explanation: Because these diseases creep up slowly over time, keeping a close eye on the patient helps us catch new problems right away and step in to help.

question: Why is it dangerous to keep expired medication anywhere near active stock supplies?

options.A: It creates a high risk of accidentally administering degraded drugs to a patient
options.B: It automatically invalidates the expiry dates of neighboring boxes
options.C: It takes up space that should be used for cleaning supplies
options.D: It causes the electric lights in the storage room to flicker

explanation: Closeness to active stock increases the chance that a busy nurse will grab an expired item during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h7)

question: Which communication habit helps build healthy, positive relationships?

options.A: Keeping all emotions hidden to avoid conflict
options.B: Interrupting the speaker to show dominance
options.C: Using 'I' statements to express personal feelings
options.D: Blaming the partner for every disagreement

explanation: Spot on! Saying 'I feel...' instead of 'You always...' stops the other person from getting defensive and opens the door to honest conversation.

question: Why do many teenage girls avoid going to health clinics for reproductive health issues?

options.A: Mandatory laws requiring parental permission for checkups
options.B: A complete absence of physical illnesses during teenage years
options.C: Fear of judgment and stigma from staff or community members
options.D: The belief that clinics only treat elderly patients

explanation: Exactly. Fear of being gossiped about or judged stops many young people from getting the medical help they truly need.

question: What does peripheral resistance refer to in the circulatory system?

options.A: Fluid loss through capillary pores
options.B: Friction of blood against vessel walls
options.C: The pumping strength of the left atrium
options.D: The speed of oxygen binding to hemoglobin

explanation: Peripheral resistance is the drag or friction blood experiences as it travels through the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h6)

question: Which drug is given immediately for a patient experiencing severe anaphylactic shock?

options.A: Furosemide
options.B: Paracetamol
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Epinephrine given in the muscle acts fast to open up airways and reverse dangerous swelling and drops in blood pressure.

question: When should a nurse ideally start rehab care for a hospitalized patient?

options.A: As soon as the patient is medically stable
options.B: After the patient is completely discharged home
options.C: When the family requests assistance with daily tasks
options.D: Only when all physical therapy orders are finished

explanation: Great thinking! Starting early stops stiff joints and weak muscles before they even start.

question: What is the main purpose of doing a colonoscopy?

options.A: Viewing the entire colon lining and removing polyps
options.B: Flushing out impacted stool from the small intestine
options.C: Measuring the exact pressure inside the stomach
options.D: Checking liver enzymes through a small tissue sample

explanation: Well done! A colonoscopy allows the doctor to use a tiny camera scope to look directly at the large bowel lining, take tissue samples, or safely remove growths.

question: You are getting ready to hang a unit of blood and notice your patient has a mild fever. What is your best first step?

options.A: Administer ice packs to reduce the temperature and infuse quickly
options.B: Report the fever to the physician before starting the transfusion
options.C: Cancel the transfusion entirely without notifying the doctor
options.D: Proceed with the transfusion and give paracetamol afterward

explanation: Always loop the doctor in! Since fever is also a top sign of a transfusion reaction, we need a baseline check so we don't confuse a pre-existing fever with a reaction later.

question: If local surveys show an increase in unmet family planning needs among teenagers, what is the best nursing action?

options.A: Close the adolescent clinic to prevent community backlash
options.B: Establish youth-friendly reproductive health education and confidential counseling
options.C: Assume the survey data is incorrect and take no action
options.D: Report the teenagers to local law enforcement authorities immediately

explanation: Teens need a safe, judgment-free space to ask questions. Setting up youth-friendly, confidential clinics helps them get the right guidance without fear.

question: A male patient with severe chest pain waited three days to visit the clinic because he felt he had to 'be strong' for his family. Which concept best explains this delay?

options.A: An innate genetic flaw in male chromosome pairing
options.B: Socially constructed gender roles influencing health-seeking behavior
options.C: A standard physiological reaction to low blood pressure
options.D: An intersex hormonal imbalance affecting pain receptors

explanation: You're doing great! Traditional masculine expectations to be stoic can sadly stop men from seeking quick medical attention.

question: An elderly patient with unsteady balance is admitted to your ward. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Tie the patient securely to the bed to prevent movement
options.B: Ensure the call bell is within reach and pathways are clear
options.C: Restrict all out-of-bed activity for the entire hospital stay
options.D: Turn off the room lights at night so the patient sleeps

explanation: Brilliant! Keeping pathways free of clutter and making sure they can easily call for help keeps them safe without using harsh restraints.

question: During a quick nursing assessment, which of these is an early warning sign that a patient is struggling to breathe?

options.A: Use of accessory muscles to breathe
options.B: Warm and dry skin on the extremities
options.C: A slow and irregular heart rate
options.D: Normal resting respiratory rate

explanation: Spot on! When breathing gets tough, patients start using their neck and shoulder muscles to help pull air in.

question: What is the primary physiological defect in Type 1 diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Temporary glucose intolerance during pregnancy
options.B: Target cell resistance to normal insulin levels
options.C: Excessive glucagon production by the liver
options.D: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells

explanation: Type 1 diabetes happens because the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and destroys the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h1)

question: How many main pillars make up the core safe motherhood framework?

options.A: Two
options.B: Eight
options.C: Four
options.D: Six

explanation: That's correct! The four pillars are family planning, antenatal care, safe delivery (obstetric care), and postnatal care.

question: Why do nurses care about catching cervical irritation early?

options.A: It prevents simple discomfort from progressing to chronic or ascending infections.
options.B: It immediately normalizes hormonal fluctuations during the menstrual cycle.
options.C: It guarantees that surgical intervention will never be required.
options.D: It completely eliminates the future risk of all pelvic inflammatory diseases.

explanation: Exactly! Catching inflammation early stops it from traveling up into the upper reproductive tract where it can cause bigger problems.

question: What is the primary characteristic of a malignant neoplasm compared to a benign one?

options.A: It invades nearby tissues and spreads to other parts of the body.
options.B: It stops growing entirely after a few weeks without treatment.
options.C: It only affects older adults and ignores younger populations.
options.D: It stays localized in one spot and never grows very large.

explanation: Malignant neoplasms are cancerous because they can break away, invade surrounding structures, and travel through the blood or lymph system. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h1)

question: How does your skin help cool you down on a very hot day?

options.A: By constricting surface blood vessels to trap heat
options.B: By shedding the outer epidermal layer to release trapped heat
options.C: By increasing subcutaneous fat thickness to block external warmth
options.D: By producing sweat and widening blood vessels near the surface

explanation: You've got this! Sweat cools you as it evaporates, and widening your blood vessels lets warm blood flow close to the surface so heat can escape.

question: Why is writing clear, real-time notes so important in emergency nursing?

options.A: It provides a clear legal record of all care provided
options.B: Doctors use the nurse's notes to diagnose diseases
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital insurance claim gets paid

explanation: Good documentation protects your patient's ongoing care and acts as legal proof in court of the great nursing care you delivered.

question: In a healthy human body, where do normal prion proteins naturally live?

options.A: Along the lining of the gut
options.B: On the membranes of neurons
options.C: Inside red blood cells
options.D: Within the fluid of joints

explanation: You got it! Normal prions hang out peacefully on the surface membranes of our nerve cells. It's only when they change shape that trouble starts.

question: Why do nurses need to provide individualized care instead of treating every pregnant woman the exact same way?

options.A: It ensures that all pregnant women take the exact same supplements
options.B: Medical doctors refuse to see patients who follow standard routines
options.C: Standard hospital guidelines are illegal to use in public clinics
options.D: Every woman has unique social, cultural, and physiological needs

explanation: No two mothers are alike! Factoring in her background, culture, and unique body helps you give care that truly fits her life.

question: What tool do public health officials mainly use to track FGM rates across Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Customs Import Records
options.B: Primary School Attendance Sheets
options.C: Demographic and Health Surveys
options.D: National Electoral Voting Registers

explanation: Correct! Health surveys give us reliable statistical data on how common FGM is and how trends are shifting across different regions.

question: What major staffing headache in Nigerian healthcare do polyvalent nurses help solve?

options.A: A lack of patients seeking medical treatment
options.B: Shortages of specialized nursing personnel in facilities
options.C: An oversupply of doctors in rural health centers
options.D: Excessive funding for primary health care clinics

explanation: You got it! They are a wonderful solution for bridging the gap where specialized nurses are hard to find.

question: When using a bulb syringe to clear a newborn's airway, which part should you suction first?

options.A: Mouth
options.B: Pharynx
options.C: Trachea
options.D: Nose

explanation: Always suction the mouth before the nose! If you do the nose first, the baby might gasp and accidentally inhale any fluid sitting in their mouth.

question: What is the most common cause of peripheral neuropathy worldwide?

options.A: Carpal tunnel syndrome
options.B: Diabetes mellitus
options.C: Guillain-Barré syndrome
options.D: Vitamin C deficiency

explanation: When blood sugar stays high over a long time, it slowly damages the tiny blood vessels that feed our nerves. That's why diabetes is the top cause of neuropathy!

question: A nurse gives a patient pain medication. What is the best next step?

options.A: Instructing the patient to stop pressing the call bell
options.B: Documenting that the pain is completely gone forever
options.C: Reassessing the patient's pain level after a short interval
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately to save hospital beds

explanation: Always close the loop! Checking back in lets you know if the drug is actually doing its job or if the patient needs extra help.

question: What do we call a cancer that starts in the epithelial tissue lining body surfaces?

options.A: Sarcoma
options.B: Myeloma
options.C: Leukemia
options.D: Carcinoma

explanation: You're doing great! Carcinomas are the most common type of cancer because they start in the skin and the cells lining our internal organs and body surfaces.

question: Why must a nurse make sure a patient takes off any metal jewelry before an X-ray?

options.A: Metal items will permanently ruin the X-ray film
options.B: Metal objects block the rays and create artifacts
options.C: Metal interferes with the magnetic field used
options.D: Metal can absorb radiation and burn the skin

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely, leaving bright white spots on the image. These spots can hide fractures, so taking off jewelry or metal items is a quick safety step you won't want to miss.

question: A patient on long-term traction complains of sudden calf pain, swelling, and warmth in their other leg. What should you suspect?

options.A: Normal muscle fatigue
options.B: Superficial skin abrasion
options.C: Deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Early pin site infection

explanation: Spot on! When patients can't move around much, blood flow slows down, putting them at risk for a blood clot (DVT) in the calf. Always stay alert for this!

question: A patient's right thumb starts twitching, then the whole arm shakes, and soon the entire body is involved with a loss of consciousness. What is this called?

options.A: A primary generalized myoclonic twitch
options.B: A benign febrile convulsion
options.C: Focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizure
options.D: A purely generalized absence seizure

explanation: You nailed it! Starting in one spot ('focal') and spreading to take over the whole brain ('bilateral') describes this exact progression.

question: Why must every item inside the home visiting kit have a specific, designated place?

options.A: To ensure the patient can easily borrow the tools
options.B: To comply with fashion standards for community nurses
options.C: To make the bag heavier and more professional looking
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination and save time during emergencies

explanation: Organizing the bag strictly separates clean items from used ones, stopping the spread of germs while keeping care efficient. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h2)

question: What term describes the visible, public customs and community rituals people use to express grief after someone dies?

options.A: Mourning
options.B: Bereavement
options.C: Perceived loss
options.D: Anticipatory grief

explanation: Well done! Mourning is all about the outward, shared actions and cultural rituals we use to honor a life and process our grief publicly.

question: Why can a problem at the very start of hormone production affect multiple different hormone levels?

options.A: All sex hormones share a common pathway originating from cholesterol.
options.B: Adrenal glands stop producing blood entirely.
options.C: Receptors on target tissues become permanently blocked.
options.D: The liver destroys excess hormones when one pathway fails.

explanation: Since all sex hormones branch out from the same starting block (cholesterol), a hiccup early in the chain reaction alters everything downstream. Makes total sense when you picture it like a branching river!

question: How does a nurse best show public health advocacy regarding breathing disorders?

options.A: Doing deep lung biopsies in local health clinics
options.B: Isolating every single person with a seasonal flu
options.C: Supporting policies that cut down air pollution and tobacco use
options.D: Prescribing strong bronchodilators to people in the neighborhood

explanation: Advocacy goes beyond the hospital bedside. Nurses advocate by supporting healthier environments, clean air policies, and community tobacco control.

question: Which of these is a classic sign of a torn urethra in a male patient?

options.A: Painless swelling of the scrotum
options.B: Sudden uncontrollable diarrhea
options.C: Blood at the urethral meatus
options.D: Yellowing of the eye sclera

explanation: Seeing a bit of blood right at the opening of the penis tells us immediately that the urethra might be torn. Great clinical clue to keep in mind!

question: A patient on the ward has a normal blood pressure but a rising heart rate and an increased breathing rate. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The room temperature is simply too high.
options.B: The patient is recovering well and ready for discharge.
options.C: The patient is compensating for an early internal complication.
options.D: The monitoring equipment needs to be replaced immediately.

explanation: Changes in heart and breathing rates are early distress signals that show up before blood pressure finally gives way. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h4)

question: How do blood vessel (vascular) diseases lead to erectile dysfunction?

options.A: By causing excessive testosterone production in the testes
options.B: By blocking the normal production of seminal fluid
options.C: By destroying the nerves of the cremasteric muscle
options.D: By impairing adequate blood flow into the cavernous tissues

explanation: You got it! An erection needs good, healthy blood flow to fill the tissues. If vascular disease gets in the way, that flow is restricted.

question: What is a pathologic fracture?

options.A: A break occurring in a bone weakened by an underlying disease
options.B: A minor hairline crack caused by repetitive athletic training
options.C: A clean break resulting from a high-speed motor vehicle crash
options.D: A fracture caused strictly by a direct blow from a blunt object

explanation: Pathologic fractures happen because an existing disease like cancer or osteoporosis has already made the bone fragile. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h2)

question: What does arterial bleeding typically look like?

options.A: Clear fluid mixed with streaks of old blood
options.B: Slowly oozing blood that stops without pressure
options.C: Bright red blood that spurts with each heartbeat
options.D: Dark red blood that flows in a steady stream

explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood under high pressure straight from the heart, causing it to spurt when they are cut. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why is ovarian cancer often tricky to catch in its early stages?

options.A: The ovaries are located deep in the pelvis and early tumors rarely cause symptoms
options.B: Symptoms always mimic a common urinary tract infection
options.C: Blood tests routinely miss the specific markers of early ovarian growth
options.D: Ovarian tissue does not develop abnormal cells until late adulthood

explanation: Because the pelvis gives the ovaries plenty of room to stretch, tumors can grow quite a bit before causing any noticeable pain or pressure.

question: What is the first thing a nurse should check before starting a teaching session?

options.A: The cost of printing handouts
options.B: The personal hobbies of the patient
options.C: The patient's readiness to learn
options.D: The availability of colorful posters

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is in severe pain or exhausted, teaching won't stick. Always check if they are ready first.

question: What term describes the use of multiple medications simultaneously, which is common in older adults?

options.A: Enteric coating
options.B: Polypharmacy
options.C: Aspiration risk
options.D: First-pass effect

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to the concurrent use of multiple drugs by a patient, which frequently happens in geriatric care and raises the risk of drug interactions. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a prerenal cause of acute kidney injury?

options.A: Direct toxicity to the kidney tubules from certain drugs
options.B: Severe inflammation of the glomeruli inside the kidney
options.C: A large kidney stone blocking the ureter completely
options.D: Severe dehydration from heavy vomiting and diarrhea

explanation: Prerenal causes involve a lack of adequate blood flow to the kidneys, often due to fluid loss like severe dehydration or shock. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which waste product from muscle breakdown is checked in lab tests to see how well kidneys are working?

options.A: Creatinine
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: Spot on! Creatinine is a normal waste product from our muscles. If the kidneys aren't filtering well, this level builds up in the blood.

question: Why is FGM often linked to a young girl's future marriage prospects in some societies?

options.A: Uncut women are frequently labeled unmarriageable by local standards
options.B: Traditional wedding planners refuse to work with uncut families
options.C: Local marriage laws forbid ceremonies for unaltered brides
options.D: Grooms require medical certificates proving childhood surgery

explanation: Spot on! Community stigma says only cut women are worthy of marriage, pressuring families to comply.

question: A nurse is about to administer a high-alert medication like IV heparin. What should be done first?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to document the administration
options.B: An independent double-check of the dose with another qualified nurse
options.C: Asking the patient to guess what the medication is used for
options.D: Hiding the medication package so other staff members cannot see it

explanation: High-alert drugs can easily cause severe harm if miscalculated. Always get a second nurse to independently verify the dose before giving it!

question: Why is the brain hit the hardest when someone experiences asphyxia?

options.A: It has a high metabolic rate and constant oxygen demand
options.B: It produces its own oxygen through cellular division
options.C: It stores large reserves of backup oxygen
options.D: It is protected by cerebrospinal fluid that blocks toxins

explanation: The brain is a busy organ that constantly demands oxygen. When that supply cuts off, brain cells start struggling almost immediately. Great job reviewing this!

question: Which blood vessel carries nutrient-rich blood straight from the intestines to the liver?

options.A: Portal vein
options.B: Renal artery
options.C: Inferior vena cava
options.D: Hepatic vein

explanation: You got this! The portal vein acts like a direct highway taking blood filled with digested nutrients straight from your gut to the liver for processing.

question: Which of these is a well-known long-term health complication of Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Enhanced hormonal balance during adolescence
options.B: Permanent immunity to sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Obstructed labor and chronic pelvic infections
options.D: Complete elimination of menstrual cramps

explanation: FGM leaves behind scar tissue that can cause long-term pain and make childbirth terribly dangerous later in life. It's a key practice public health nurses actively campaign against.

question: Which chemical messengers in the brain usually get thrown out of balance during neurodegeneration?

options.A: Blood proteins like albumin and globulin
options.B: Neurotransmitters like dopamine and serotonin
options.C: Digestive enzymes like pepsin and amylase
options.D: Respiratory gases like oxygen and carbon dioxide

explanation: Spot on! When brain cells die off, it messes up neurotransmitters like dopamine and serotonin, which directly change mood, behavior, and thinking. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h2)

question: How do abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich maneuver) help a choking person?

options.A: They drain trapped fluid from the lower lungs
options.B: They force trapped air upward to pop the object out
options.C: They help the heart pump blood faster
options.D: They help the patient relax their vocal cords

explanation: Abdominal thrusts squeeze the diaphragm upward. This creates a quick puff of artificial air from the lungs that acts like a cough to push the blockage out.

question: How is a patient usually positioned immediately after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Flat in bed
options.B: Trendelenburg position
options.C: High Fowler's position
options.D: Standing up and walking

explanation: Spot on! Lying flat helps the tiny puncture hole seal up and lowers the chance of a stubborn spinal headache.

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop the spread of infection?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns
options.B: Hand hygiene
options.C: Routine room painting
options.D: Using plastic aprons

explanation: Proper handwashing or alcohol rub use removes transient microbes from hands, preventing cross-contamination between patients. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h4)

question: A patient is admitted with severe vomiting and diarrhea. Which imbalance are they most at risk for developing?

options.A: Fluid and electrolyte imbalance
options.B: Excessive weight gain
options.C: Permanent high blood pressure
options.D: Chronic respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Exactly! Vomiting and diarrhea flush out body fluids and essential minerals super fast, leaving the patient low on water and electrolytes.

question: Why do some degenerative disorder patients lose weight rapidly even when they eat normal meals?

options.A: The stomach completely stops absorbing any nutrients
options.B: Kidneys process and excrete all calories as pure water
options.C: Medications permanently block the sensation of hunger
options.D: A hypermetabolic state caused by abnormal muscle activity

explanation: When muscles twitch or stay tight all day, they burn up massive amounts of energy—just like running a car engine in neutral!

question: What makes a modern modular operating theatre special in terms of structure?

options.A: Seamless, pre-fabricated panels that resist bacterial growth
options.B: Wooden flooring to absorb sound and reduce echoes
options.C: Traditional painted concrete walls that are easy to repaint
options.D: Open windows to allow natural sunlight during daytime surgery

explanation: Spot on! Modular theatres use smooth, factory-made panels so there are no tiny cracks or corners where stubborn germs and dust can hide.

question: Which condition is a strict, absolute 'no-go' for giving radioactive iodine (I-131) therapy?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Advanced age
options.C: Mild tachycardia
options.D: Pregnancy

explanation: Radioactive iodine can cross the placenta and harm the baby's developing thyroid, so pregnancy is an absolute contraindication.

question: What is the main cause of Respiratory Distress Syndrome in a premature baby?

options.A: A weak and underdeveloped heart muscle
options.B: An infection in the urinary tract
options.C: A lack of pulmonary surfactant
options.D: Swallowing too much amniotic fluid

explanation: Without enough surfactant to keep them open, the baby's tiny air sacs stick together and collapse. Knowing this helps you understand why we push for steroid coverage!

question: Which monitoring finding tells you that the mum's distress is starting to affect the baby?

options.A: Late decelerations on the fetal monitor
options.B: A normal, stable baseline fetal heart rate
options.C: Moderate short-term heart rate variability
options.D: Accelerations with maternal movement

explanation: Spotting late decelerations is a red flag for poor placental blood flow, often tied back to maternal stress and tight blood vessels.

question: In nursing, what does the term 'self-care deficit' mean?

options.A: An impaired ability to perform daily activities like bathing and grooming
options.B: Lacking school training on health habits
options.C: Not having enough money to buy soap
options.D: A patient refusing help from any health worker

explanation: You got this! A self-care deficit simply means a patient struggles to do daily tasks like washing or dressing on their own.

question: Why are gentle, early movements introduced after the initial swelling of a sprain goes down?

options.A: To force the torn ends of the ligament to stretch beyond their normal length
options.B: To prevent joint stiffness and promote healthy ligament fiber alignment
options.C: To completely dissolve any remaining bruises within twenty-four hours
options.D: To replace the need for pain relief medications during recovery

explanation: Controlled movement helps new collagen fibers line up correctly as they heal, preventing stiffness and long-term weakness.

question: What important advice should a nurse give a heart failure patient about managing fluids at home?

options.A: Stop taking your water pills whenever you feel thirsty
options.B: Drink at least four liters of water every single morning
options.C: Weigh yourself daily and report sudden weight gains
options.D: Avoid all physical movement to save body water

explanation: Brilliant! Stepping on the scale every day is the easiest way for a patient to catch fluid buildup before it turns into breathing trouble.

question: A patient scheduled for a procedure with mild sedation asks for a glass of water an hour beforehand. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Explain that fasting guidelines must be followed to prevent aspiration during sedation.
options.B: Ignore the question because fluid intake does not affect anesthesia safety.
options.C: Tell the patient to drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated before the test.
options.D: Allow the patient to drink a small cup of water since it is just a liquid.

explanation: Fasting (NPO) keeps the stomach empty so the patient doesn't accidentally choke or inhale stomach contents while sedated. Safety first!

question: How soon can a woman get pregnant again after having an abortion?

options.A: Only after her normal monthly period returns
options.B: After waiting at least six months
options.C: As early as two weeks
options.D: Not until a full year has passed

explanation: Ovulation can bounce back super fast after an abortion, so family planning counseling before discharge is a must. Keep this in mind for patient education!

question: Why does the valve at the bottom of the esophagus close tightly after food enters the stomach?

options.A: To signal the brain that a meal has finished
options.B: To stop acidic stomach contents from flowing backward
options.C: To prevent air from entering the abdominal cavity
options.D: To trap food in the esophagus for further chewing

explanation: Spot on! This little muscular gatekeeper stops harsh stomach acid from splashing back up and burning the food pipe.

question: In the CAUTION mnemonic for warning signs of cancer, what does the letter 'U' stand for?

options.A: Urinary frequency and burning
options.B: Ulceration of the skin surface
options.C: Unusual bleeding or discharge
options.D: Unexplained upper abdominal pain

explanation: You nailed it! The 'U' stands for unusual bleeding or discharge from anywhere in the body. It's an important red flag that needs checking.

question: A patient taking antibiotics for an H. pylori ulcer asks if they can stop taking the pills once the pain stops. What is the best nurse response?

options.A: Take half the remaining dose over the next few days
options.B: Stop the pills immediately to prevent drug side effects
options.C: Switch to antacids once the burning sensation stops
options.D: Complete all pills to ensure the bacteria is fully cleared

explanation: You're thinking like a true nurse! Stopping antibiotics early lets the toughest bacteria survive, leading to drug resistance and a returning ulcer.

question: What is the most common correctable physical cause of male infertility?

options.A: Varicocele
options.B: Testicular torsion
options.C: Klinefelter syndrome
options.D: Cryptorchidism

explanation: A varicocele is an enlarged set of veins in the scrotum that doctors can surgically repair to help restore normal fertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: Which professional has special training to help couples work through emotional and intimacy problems?

options.A: Orthopedic surgeon
options.B: Emergency room registrar
options.C: Phlebotomy technician
options.D: Certified sex therapist

explanation: Sex therapists have specialized training to guide couples through psychological and emotional intimacy bumps on the road.

question: Which type of drug crosses biological cell membranes the easiest?

options.A: Fat-soluble molecules
options.B: Water-soluble salts
options.C: Highly charged ions
options.D: Large protein molecules

explanation: Cell membranes are made of fats (lipids), so fat-friendly (lipophilic) drugs slide right through them without needing any special ticket!

question: Which common bacterium is a major cause of long-term gastritis and stomach ulcers?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Helicobacter pylori
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.D: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation: Well done! Helicobacter pylori (or H. pylori) loves to hang out in the stomach lining, causing irritation and stubborn ulcers over time.

question: Why do nurses use the nursing process in patient care?

options.A: To speed up hospital discharge procedures
options.B: To provide a structured framework for delivering individualized care
options.C: To replace the need for direct communication with physicians
options.D: To diagnose complex medical diseases independently

explanation: Spot on! The nursing process helps you organize patient care into clear, step-by-step actions tailored to each person's unique needs. You've got this!

question: What is the main job of a medical-surgical nurse?

options.A: Managing administrative budgets for hospital wards and clinics
options.B: Caring for adult patients with various medical illnesses and surgical needs
options.C: Delivering emergency psychiatric interventions in crisis centers
options.D: Providing specialized surgical operations inside the operating theater

explanation: You'll see med-surg nursing everywhere in the hospital! It's all about looking after adults dealing with medical conditions or bouncing back from surgery. You've got this!

question: What is a common misconception patients sometimes hold about essential drugs?

options.A: They think essential drugs are only sold in overseas luxury clinics
options.B: They refuse to take them because they taste too sweet
options.C: They assume essential drugs can cure every known genetic disorder
options.D: They believe essential drugs are inferior because they are affordable

explanation: Because essential medicines are reasonably priced generics, some people wrongly assume they lack potency compared to expensive brands. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: How does chronic cervicitis mainly differ from acute cervicitis?

options.A: It involves long-standing immune cell changes in the tissue.
options.B: It presents with sudden, severe pus-like discharge.
options.C: It never requires any medical or nursing intervention.
options.D: It is always caused by viral agents rather than bacteria.

explanation: Think of acute as sudden and angry with quick pus, while chronic is a longer-lasting, low-grade immune response in the tissue.

question: Why is fluoroscopy a key component of a barium swallow test?

options.A: It provides real-time moving images of swallowing and peristalsis
options.B: It permanently removes small blockages in the throat
options.C: It measures the exact pH levels inside the stomach
options.D: It checks the patient's blood pressure throughout the scan

explanation: Unlike standard still X-rays, fluoroscopy acts like an X-ray movie, letting the radiologist watch how food and liquid move down the throat in real time. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which imaging test is the absolute go-to choice for getting a clear picture of brain and spinal tumors?

options.A: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
options.B: Bone densitometry scan
options.C: Standard chest X-ray
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: Spot on! MRI gives doctors the sharpest, most detailed look at soft tissues like the brain and spinal cord, making it the favorite tool for spotting nervous system growths.

question: What is the primary reason for diluting a highly concentrated intravenous medication?

options.A: To change the chemical class of the drug
options.B: To make the medication expire much slower
options.C: To eliminate the need for sterile technique
options.D: To reduce irritation to the blood vessels

explanation: High concentrations of certain drugs can damage vein walls and cause severe pain or tissue injury. Diluting them lowers this risk. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why is it important to watch the client's face during passive exercises?

options.A: To check if they are watching the television
options.B: To spot hidden pain or distress when they cannot speak well
options.C: To check how fast their hair is growing
options.D: To see if they need spectacles to read

explanation: Wonderful! Many patients can't tell you when it hurts, so a quick wince or frown on their face tells you everything you need to know.

question: Which of the following is NOT a core ethical principle guiding palliative nursing care?

options.A: Autonomy
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Punitive dominance
options.D: Non-maleficence

explanation: Punitive dominance is made up! Nursing ethics are built on principles like autonomy, beneficence, and non-maleficence. Easy point for you!

question: Why does HIV specifically attack CD4+ T-cells and macrophages?

options.A: These cells circulate faster than other blood cells in the human body
options.B: These cells produce large amounts of viral protease that activate the virus
options.C: These cells ingest the virus to destroy it permanently before it multiplies
options.D: These cells express surface receptors and co-receptors that the virus needs to enter

explanation: You got it! HIV needs specific matching receptors (like CD4) on the cell surface to hook on and gain entry. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h2)

question: Which receptors detect a sudden drop in blood pressure during a haemorrhage?

options.A: Pain receptors
options.B: Chemoreceptors
options.C: Baroreceptors
options.D: Thermoreceptors

explanation: Baroreceptors are pressure sensors located in major blood vessels that notice when blood pressure falls and alert the nervous system. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h3)

question: A patient who just had cataract surgery asks why they must avoid heavy lifting. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Heavy lifting causes secondary cataracts
options.B: Bending over can cause pink eye
options.C: Lifting dries out the surface of your eye
options.D: Straining raises your eye pressure and can pop the healing stitches

explanation: Spot on! Straining, heavy lifting, or bending down spikes the pressure inside the eye, which can easily damage fresh surgical cuts.

question: When you are checking if a patient is fully 'oriented,' what three key things do you ask about?

options.A: Sight, hearing, and touch
options.B: Height, weight, and age
options.C: Pulse, temperature, and blood pressure
options.D: Person, place, and time

explanation: Checking person, place, and time is the classic, quick way to test if a patient's brain is alert and aware of their surroundings.

question: Why should you avoid using cold compresses to treat pain during a sickle cell crisis?

options.A: Refrigerated items increase the risk of skin breakdown over swollen joints
options.B: Cold temperatures cause blood vessels to constrict and promote further sickling
options.C: Low temperatures stop intravenous pain medications from working properly
options.D: Cold packs numb the skin so the patient cannot feel if the pain is improving

explanation: Remember: cold makes blood vessels narrow (vasoconstriction). This slows down blood flow even more, making the sickled cells clump together worse and increasing the patient's pain.

question: What is the best way to walk down the hall with a patient who has a visual impairment?

options.A: Walk behind the client and verbally give step-by-step directions
options.B: Walk side by side while holding hands tightly with the client
options.C: Push the client from behind by placing hands firmly on their shoulders
options.D: Walk slightly ahead and let the client hold onto your elbow

explanation: You've got it! Letting them hold your elbow while you lead slightly gives them physical cues for your movements and keeps them feeling secure.

question: Why does reproductive health cover mental and social well-being alongside physical health?

options.A: Mental health is legally required to be assessed before any family planning service
options.B: Emotional stress can directly alter a person's hormonal balance and fertility rates
options.C: Psychological counseling is the primary treatment for most reproductive tract infections
options.D: Reproductive choices and experiences deeply affect a person's emotional life and social standing

explanation: You know how personal family and reproductive matters are. Because they touch our deepest emotions and community standing, mental and social health are just as vital as physical health!

question: Why might a struggling family find it hard to follow advice about eating a balanced diet?

options.A: Local health nurses refuse to give them recipe books
options.B: Daily survival and food costs take priority over long-term health
options.C: Traditional beliefs forbid the eating of vegetables
options.D: They lack basic interest in learning about nutrition

explanation: When money is tight, finding food for today always comes before thinking about long-term wellness. Empathy is key here!

question: What does a pacemaker 'failure to capture' mean?

options.A: Pacing spikes show on the monitor, but the heart does not beat in response
options.B: The device fails to notice the patient's own heartbeat and fires at the wrong time
options.C: The wires disconnect from the skin surface outside the chest wall
options.D: The internal battery runs out completely and the heart stops instantly

explanation: Failure to capture means the pacemaker is sending out the signal (the spike), but the heart muscle isn't responding to it. You are getting the hang of ECG concepts!

question: Which health challenge do rural communities face most often?

options.A: Long travel times to reach comprehensive healthcare
options.B: High rates of industrial air pollution and overcrowding
options.C: An overabundance of specialized tertiary hospitals
options.D: Excessive noise pollution from heavy urban traffic

explanation: Correct! Distance and poor roads often make getting to a well-equipped hospital a real journey for rural villagers.

question: When is the right time to change an absorbent diaper or pad for your patient?

options.A: Right before the doctor arrives for ward round
options.B: As soon as the patient complains of feeling hungry
options.C: Promptly whenever it becomes soiled or wet
options.D: Only once every twenty-four hours during the morning shift

explanation: Don't wait for a schedule if comfort and skin health are on the line. Check frequently and change diapers right away when they are wet or soiled.

question: Which inherited enzyme deficiency is a major risk factor for severe neonatal jaundice in Nigeria?

options.A: Sickle cell trait
options.B: Phenylketonuria
options.C: Lactose intolerance
options.D: G6PD deficiency

explanation: G6PD deficiency is prevalent in the region and makes newborn red cells very fragile when exposed to certain oxidative triggers like camphor. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h4)

question: What is a key focus during post-test counselling for a client who tests negative?

options.A: Discussing prevention methods and the window period
options.B: Reporting the client to local security agencies
options.C: Isolating the client from their family members
options.D: Starting immediate lifelong antiretroviral treatment

explanation: Negative results require education on staying negative and understanding that recent exposures might not show up immediately during the window period. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h3)

question: How can a nurse best check a baby's skin for a yellow tint during a physical exam?

options.A: Gently pressing the skin over a bony prominence to blanch it
options.B: Pinching a fold of skin on the baby's arm to test elasticity
options.C: Observing the baby inside a dark room using a standard flashlight
options.D: Shining a blue phototherapy light directly onto the infant's abdomen

explanation: Pressing gently over a bone clears the surface blood for a second, making the underlying yellow bilirubin tint much easier to spot. Simple and effective bedside nursing!

question: What dangerous habit must nurses watch out for when patients use axillary crutches?

options.A: Resting body weight directly on the armpits
options.B: Looking straight ahead instead of down at the floor
options.C: Holding the handgrips too loosely with the palms
options.D: Walking too slowly during hallway exercises

explanation: Good catch! Resting weight in the armpits can smash nerves and blood vessels. Patients must always support their weight with their hands.

question: What is the primary objective of family planning counseling?

options.A: To eliminate population growth in developing nations completely
options.B: To force every woman of childbearing age to use hormonal contraception
options.C: To promote permanent surgical sterilization for all young couples
options.D: To help clients make informed choices about child spacing and family size

explanation: Family planning empowers clients with information to choose their preferred method safely and voluntarily. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which ventilator mode takes over completely, giving a set rate and volume without letting the patient take spontaneous breaths?

options.A: Continuous Positive Airway Pressure
options.B: Pressure Support Ventilation
options.C: Controlled Mandatory Ventilation
options.D: Synchronized Intermittent Mandatory Ventilation

explanation: Great try! Controlled Mandatory Ventilation (CMV) handles the entire breathing cycle for the patient without waiting for them to trigger a breath.

question: What is a simple, important instruction to give a patient right before the IVP scan starts?

options.A: Drink two large cups of water.
options.B: Take your scheduled metformin dose.
options.C: Lie flat on your stomach for an hour.
options.D: Empty your bladder completely.

explanation: Asking the patient to pee right before the test gives us a clean baseline image of an empty bladder.

question: A patient expresses deep worry that their life had no meaning and feels utterly forgotten. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Tell them not to worry because everyone feels sad sometimes
options.B: Sit quietly, listen attentively, and validate their feelings
options.C: Change the subject immediately to cheer them up
options.D: Administer a strong sedative to make them sleep

explanation: Allowing patients to voice deep spiritual or existential worries without judgment offers profound comfort. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the foramen ovale in a baby's heart before birth?

options.A: Connecting the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava to bypass the liver
options.B: Allowing blood to flow from the right atrium directly into the left atrium
options.C: Preventing maternal blood cells from entering the foetal heart chambers
options.D: Directing deoxygenated blood from the upper body back to the placenta

explanation: Spot on! The foramen ovale is a little flap-like door between the heart's upper chambers that lets oxygen-rich blood skip the right ventricle and lungs. You're doing brilliantly!

question: What usually happens to a patient's pulse rate when their body temperature goes up?

options.A: The heart rate goes down
options.B: The pulse becomes weak and irregular
options.C: The heart rate stays completely normal
options.D: The heart rate goes up

explanation: Correct! As body temperature climbs, the metabolism speeds up, making the heart beat faster too.

question: How does a shortened fallopian tube typically affect how a fertilized egg travels to the uterus?

options.A: It causes rapid transit, leading to early entry into the uterus
options.B: It traps the embryo permanently in the isthmus
options.C: It reverses the muscular waves pushing it backward
options.D: It completely stops all ciliary movement in the tubal lining

explanation: Because there is less distance to travel, the fertilized egg rushes through too quickly and reaches the uterus before it is fully ready to implant.

question: Which of these is NOT checked during a standard surgical time-out?

options.A: The exact surgical site and body part
options.B: The specific procedure intended to be done
options.C: The patient's preferred religious denomination
options.D: The correct identity of the surgical patient

explanation: While respecting a patient's religion is important for holistic care, it isn't part of the quick safety checklist used to prevent wrong-site or wrong-patient surgery.

question: What do we call the emotional exhaustion and loss of care caused by long-term stress at work?

options.A: Hypothermia
options.B: Hysteria
options.C: Burnout
options.D: Hyperglycemia

explanation: Burnout is real in demanding fields like nursing. It's that feeling of complete mental and emotional tiredness from too much stress. Take care of your mental health!

question: How does using the nursing process in critical care differ from a normal ward?

options.A: Evaluation of patient outcomes is delayed until discharge to home
options.B: Planning is entirely determined by family members rather than the nurse
options.C: Steps happen in a rapid, continuous, and overlapping loop due to instability
options.D: Assessment is performed only once upon admission to the ICU

explanation: In the ICU, things move super fast! Because patients can crash at any second, you'll find yourself assessing, helping, and checking results almost all at the same time.

question: What is your very first priority as a nurse right after an incident or accident happens on the ward?

options.A: Complete the online incident report form
options.B: Assess and stabilize the patient
options.C: Interview witnesses on the ward
options.D: Notify the hospital legal department

explanation: Patient care and safety always come first before you worry about filling out forms or doing paperwork. Clinical care is king!

question: Which pathogen is most commonly transmitted through an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Tetanus spore
options.B: Malaria parasite
options.C: Streptococcus bacteria
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: Hepatitis B is highly infectious through blood and remains a major occupational risk for health workers experiencing needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why do lung problems often affect the rest of the body?

options.A: Lung infections spread directly to the brain within hours
options.B: Every organ relies heavily on a steady supply of oxygen from the lungs
options.C: Poor breathing causes the stomach to stop digesting food completely
options.D: The heart stops pumping blood when the lungs become inflamed

explanation: You got it! If the lungs aren't working well, oxygen delivery drops, and every single tissue in the body starts to suffer. Oxygen is food for our cells!

question: Your patient is heading for a lumbar puncture in 30 minutes. What is a helpful nursing action right now?

options.A: Eat a heavy meal
options.B: Walk around the hallway
options.C: Drink two liters of water
options.D: Empty their bladder

explanation: Great job! An empty bladder keeps the patient comfortable while they curl up on their side for the procedure.

question: Which of these phrases should a nurse avoid saying to a grieving family member?

options.A: "Everything happens for a reason."
options.B: "Would you like me to sit with you for a while?"
options.C: "I am here for you if you want to talk."
options.D: "It is okay to cry and feel sad right now."

explanation: Clichés like "everything happens for a reason" can feel dismissive and hurtful to someone in deep pain. Instead, just offer your quiet presence.

question: What happens to blood vessels as a person ages normally?

options.A: Complete disappearance of capillary beds
options.B: Rapid dilation and excessive blood pooling
options.C: Spontaneous regeneration of damaged valves
options.D: Loss of elasticity and increased stiffness

explanation: You got it! Over time, blood vessels lose their stretchy fibers, becoming stiffer, which naturally contributes to higher blood pressure in older adults.

question: What does the integrase enzyme do in the HIV life cycle?

options.A: It destroys circulating antibodies produced by B cells.
options.B: It manufactures new outer coats for budding virus particles.
options.C: It breaks down the outer cell wall of the host lymphocyte.
options.D: It inserts viral DNA into the host cell's genetic material.

explanation: Integrase acts like molecular glue, pasting the copied viral DNA right into the human host cell's DNA.

question: What main change happens inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli) during pneumonia?

options.A: The walls permanently stretch and lose stretchiness.
options.B: Blood flow to the lungs completely stops overnight.
options.C: Fluid, pus, and cellular debris fill up the spaces.
options.D: The breathing tubes stretch out and trap air.

explanation: As the body fights the infection, fluid and white blood cells flood the alveoli. That's why air has such a hard time getting in!

question: A grieving family member moves rapidly between intense anger at hospital staff and deep depression within the same hour. What does this behavior indicate?

options.A: Normal fluctuation through non-linear grief stages
options.B: A pathological personality disorder requiring isolation
options.C: A failure of the nursing staff to communicate clearly
options.D: An intentional attempt to manipulate caregivers

explanation: Grief is fluid, and individuals frequently move back and forth between different stages rather than following a straight line. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h2)

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall to check a patient's food intake?

options.A: It relies heavily on the patient's memory
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment
options.C: It only measures water and ignores solid food
options.D: It takes over three hours to complete

explanation: Patients easily forget small snacks or misjudge portion sizes when trying to remember everything they ate yesterday.

question: Which anti-TB drug is known to cause vision issues like optic neuritis?

options.A: Pyrazinamide
options.B: Ethambutol
options.C: Isoniazid
options.D: Rifampicin

explanation: Ethambutol can mess with the optic nerve. That's why checking a patient's eyesight and color vision during treatment is a key nursing duty!

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do before handling chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Performing hand hygiene and putting on protective gear
options.B: Informing the head physician about the cleaning schedule
options.C: Warming the chemical solution in a microwave oven
options.D: Testing the disinfectant flavor on a sterile cotton swab

explanation: Safety first! Protecting your own skin, hands, and airways from harsh chemicals is a must before you start cleaning up the ward.

question: Which sign do we often see when a patient is in the final active dying phase?

options.A: Warm, flushed skin over the entire body
options.B: Irregular breathing patterns like Cheyne-Stokes respirations
options.C: Rapid increase in blood pressure and heart rate
options.D: Sudden increase in appetite and high energy levels

explanation: As the body gently slows down, you might notice cool hands and feet, sleeping more, and irregular breathing patterns like Cheyne-Stokes. Knowing this helps you reassure the family.

question: Which nutritional issue is especially common during the rapid physical growth of adolescence?

options.A: Scurvy
options.B: Anaemia
options.C: Rickets
options.D: Goiter

explanation: Rapid growth and poor dietary habits make adolescents, especially young females, very prone to developing anaemia. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h3)

question: If a patient has severe anemia with very low hemoglobin, what is the most direct problem this causes?

options.A: Complete cessation of carbon dioxide production
options.B: Reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood
options.C: Inability of the diaphragm to contract properly
options.D: Immediate collapse of alveolar air sacs

explanation: Spot on! Fewer delivery trucks (hemoglobin) mean the blood just can't pack and carry enough oxygen to the body tissues.

question: Why is pushing an endotracheal tube 'blindly' dangerous in severe upper airway trauma?

options.A: It causes sudden high blood pressure.
options.B: It can worsen a tear and completely block the airway.
options.C: It stops intravenous fluids from working.
options.D: It permanently paralyzes the vocal cords.

explanation: Exactly right! Forcing a tube past swollen and damaged tissues can easily push through an existing tear, completely losing the airway.

question: A patient looks down and hesitates when asked about alcohol use. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Maintain a calm, non-judgmental attitude and wait patiently
options.B: Scold the patient for hiding information
options.C: Move on immediately to a different topic to avoid embarrassment
options.D: Document that the patient is being uncooperative

explanation: Showing patience and a non-judgmental stance helps build trust so the patient feels safe sharing sensitive details. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: How does losing access to school affect a young bride's future?

options.A: It makes her physically unable to speak clearly to healthcare workers
options.B: It limits her ability to earn money and understand basic health information
options.C: It forces her to move permanently to a foreign country
options.D: It guarantees she will develop severe bone disorders in old age

explanation: Well reasoned! Without education, she misses out on financial independence and health awareness, keeping her trapped in vulnerability.

question: What is the dangerous practice of using the same syringe barrel for more than one patient called?

options.A: Syringe reuse
options.B: Z-track administration
options.C: Aseptic transfer
options.D: Vial reconstitution

explanation: You nailed it! Reusing syringes—even if you change the needle—transfers microscopic amounts of blood and fluids between patients, spreading serious infections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which healthcare professional frequently acts as the central coordinator within a multidisciplinary care team for chronic degenerative conditions?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The surgical technician
options.C: The registered nurse
options.D: The billing administrator

explanation: Nurses coordinate day-to-day care and communicate patient needs across various medical specialists and therapists. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h6)

question: What physical feature is most commonly seen in Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Permanent low blood pressure and dehydration
options.B: Central obesity with a round 'moon face'
options.C: Dark bronze hyperpigmentation of the skin
options.D: Severe weight loss and profound muscle wasting

explanation: Too much cortisol changes how fat is stored in the body, leading to a characteristic round 'moon face' and extra weight packed around the trunk and upper back.

question: Which symptom is a major red flag for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy?

options.A: Painful blisters forming exclusively around the mouth
options.B: Rapid darkening of the skin over the entire body
options.C: Severe itching on the palms and soles without an initial rash
options.D: Thick crusting sores spreading across the scalp
